entry.title: Rayleigh's conjecture for vibrating plates: simpler planar proof and nonlinear extensions
entry.summary: We give a simpler proof of Nadirashvili's theorem (Rayleigh's conjecture) that among vibrating clamped plates of prescribed area in the plane, the disk has the lowest fundamental tone. The proof uses a one-shot Talenti type comparison for sign-changing solutions of the Poisson equation with mean-zero data, established in a companion paper. The comparison considers just two rearranged sources, rather than optimizing over all admissible sources as in the traditional two-ball technique. This ``paired comparison'' simplification yields immediate nonlinear extensions: the disk minimizes the clamped quotient $\|Δu\|_q/\|u\|_p$ among bounded open sets of prescribed area, for every $1\le p,q\le\infty$. Equality is characterized for $q>1$, while exceptional behavior at $q=1$ is identified. In higher dimensions, we prove ball minimality for $p=\infty$ and conjecture minimality for all $p,q$ within the compact embedding range. We also establish the corresponding interval inequality in one dimension.

entry.title: Positive Planar Measures for Spectral Pinching and the Corrected BMV Conjecture
entry.summary: We prove the corrected Bessis--Moussa--Villani pinching conjecture for all symmetrized word averages. For Hermitian matrices $A,B$ and $D=E_A(B)$, we construct a positive compactly supported measure $ζ_{A,B}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ such that \[ \Tr f(xA+yB)-\Tr f(xA+yD) =y^2\int_{\mathbb R^2}f''(xa+yb)\,dζ_{A,B}(a,b). \] Its total mass is $\frac12\|B-D\|_2^2$. This representation proves the corrected conjecture, including its equality cases, and gives a positive bivariate moment representation for the coefficient differences. We also derive complete monotonicity of normalized exponential pinching defects and a comparison with Lie--Trotter approximations. A one-dimensional second-order loss measure is obtained for trace-preserving conditional expectations on finite tracial von Neumann algebras. Finally, we relate $ζ_{A,B}$ to Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure by an explicit positive radial transform.

entry.title: A characterization of equality between de Branges--Rovnyak and Dirichlet spaces
entry.summary: We characterize when a de Branges--Rovnyak space coincides with a harmonically weighted Dirichlet space. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for this identification, which settles a long-standing open problem. We illustrate the result with several examples, that include measures supported on uncountable sets.

entry.title: The Keller problem for the lowest positive eigenvalue of Dirac operators with Lorentz scalar potentials
entry.summary: We study the Keller problem for the Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_m - Vβ$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and minimize its lowest positive eigenvalue over all potentials $V$ with prescribed $L^p$ norm. We prove that optimal potentials always exist and that the corresponding eigenspinors solve the nonlinear Soler equation. This provides a variational proof of existence of solitary waves for this equation. We prove that there are no zero modes for such operators in dimensions $1$ and $2$, and conjecture that zero mode may exist in dimension $3$. In dimension $d = 2$, we provide numerical evidence that the optimal potentials concentrate on flower-shape regions, which are not necessarily radial, showing that Faber--Krahn type results may fail for such Dirac operators. In dimension $1$, all quantities are explicit.

entry.title: Breiman's conjecture and normalized jumps of subordinators
entry.summary: We prove Breiman's conjecture under the first-moment assumption. Let $Y_1,Y_2,\ldots$ be iid nonnegative random variables with $\mathbb P\{Y_1>0\}>0$, normalized by their sum. If the resulting randomly weighted sum converges to a nondegenerate law for one fixed integrable, nonconstant mark distribution, then the tail of $Y_1$ is regularly varying. More generally, any full-sequence limit for one such mark, including a constant limit, determines the asymptotic regime of the ranked weights: one big jump, a Poisson$\unicode{x2013}$Dirichlet partition, or dust. It consequently determines the limit for every integrable mark, with convergence in the $1$-Wasserstein metric, and the limits of independently marked empirical measures. The inverse step is based on a countable power-sum theorem: signed Fourier$\unicode{x2013}$Mellin identities extract a positive limiting expected power sum from one nondegenerate marked limit, without a moment of order greater than one. A ratio$\unicode{x2013}$Tauberian argument then recovers the tail index. The same method classifies ratios formed from the marked jumps of a nonzero, unkilled, driftless subordinator at zero and at infinity, assuming infinite activity at zero. A nondegenerate limit is equivalent to regular variation of the Lévy tail with index in $(-1,0]$. A constant limit is equivalent to disappearance of the largest normalized jump, or, analytically, to slow variation of the integrated Lévy tail. The latter condition need not imply regular variation of the Lévy tail with index $-1$. A Cauchy-mark example shows that the conclusion can fail without integrability of the mark.

entry.title: A Sharp Bound of Crossing Limit Cycle for Planar piecewise linear Systems with a Straight Switching Line
entry.summary: Determining the maximum number of crossing limit cycles in planar discontinuous piecewise linear systems separated by a straight line is a central problem in nonsmooth dynamical systems and a natural piecewise-linear counterpart of Hilbert's sixteenth problem, yet its sharp uniform upper bound has long remained an open problem. In this paper, we prove that any such system admits at most three crossing limit cycles. Combined with known examples realizing three crossing limit cycles, this result establishes that three is the sharp uniform upper bound.

entry.title: Almost Periodicity Properties Arising From the Sodin-Yuditskii Theory
entry.summary: The Kotani-Last problem and the Deift conjecture are two well known statements, which both concern the almost periodicity properties of the functions under consideration, and which have both been disproved in their original formulation, which involves Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity. To contrast these disproofs, and to further elucidate the essence of these two challenging problems, we establish positive results regarding each of them by showing that Weyl almost periodicity can be deduced whenever the Sodin-Yuditskii setup can be implemented. The latter requires that the Schrödinger operator associated with the function in question has purely absolutely continuous spectral measure and a spectrum with finite total gap length and the Parreau-Widom property. We also show that the known examples for which Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity has been shown or suggested to fail in the context of the Deift conjecture are in fact Weyl almost periodic. As a result, an accordingly modified version of the Deift conjecture remains a tantalizing open problem.

entry.title: A sharpened $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate for even initial data
entry.summary: It is well known that $u_0 \in L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ is an extremizer for the $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate if and only if it is a Gaussian. We show that every extremizing sequence of even functions $\{ u_n \} \subset L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ approaches a centered Gaussian in an appropriate sense. This result follows from a certain inequality for coordinate-wise even $L^2$ functions on $\mathbb{R}^4$ conjectured by Gonçalves (2019) which we prove in this paper with the optimal constant.

entry.title: On the Propeller Conjecture
entry.summary: We simplify and improve OpenAI's proof of the propeller conjecture of Khot and Naor from 2008: the sum of the squared lengths of the Gaussian moments of any partition of Euclidean space is at most $9/(8π)$. We show equality only occurs for three 120 degree sectors in the plane (up to symmetries, measure zero changes, and taking orthogonal cross products with Euclidean space). We also remove computer assistance from the three-dimensional case of the conjecture, which previously used an epsilon net traversal.

entry.title: Berezin--Li--Yau inequalities for Aharonov--Bohm operators
entry.summary: We prove the sharp Berezin--Li--Yau inequality for Riesz means of order at least one for Aharonov--Bohm operators on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. This confirms a conjecture posed by Frank and Hansson in 2008. We also obtain an improved lower bound for individual eigenvalues and extend it to the case of magnetic potentials with bounded magnetic field. These results are then applied to deduce estimates for Riesz means of orders between zero and one, and for Aharonov--Bohm eigenvalues on product domains.

entry.title: Subsequential Version of Breiman's Conjecture
entry.summary: We study randomly weighted sums \[ T_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n X_iY_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i}, \] where $(X_i)$ and $(Y_i)$ are independent sequences of i.i.d. random variables, with nonnegative weights $Y_i$, motivated by Breiman's conjecture. We introduce the class $ISSV$ of $I$-subsequentially slowly varying tails and establish a subsequential analogue of Darling's maximum--sum theorem. This provides a subsequential generalization of Breiman's slowly varying theorem and, as a corollary, resolves the slowly varying case of his conjecture. We also establish a subsequential analogue of Breiman's nonzero-index theorem, characterizing the existence of nondegenerate subsequential limits, distinct in distribution from $X_1,$ by the failure of slow variation of the integrated tail, for weight $Y_1$ with tail distributions outside the class $ISSV$. Finally, we formulate the subsequential separation principle, prove it under a finite-second-moment assumption, and show that its general validity would imply the nonzero-index case of Breiman's conjecture.

entry.title: Compactness of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees
entry.summary: In this paper, we present a complete characterization of the compactness of arbitrary finite linear combinations of composition operators acting on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. In particular, we obtain a characterization of compactness for linear combinations satisfying the CNC. As an application, we give an affirmative answer to a conjecture raised by Choe et al. [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B 9(2022), 733--756] concerning such Hardy spaces. Furthermore, we establish the phenomenon of (double) difference cancellation for linear combinations of composition operators by constructing explicit examples.

entry.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
entry.summary: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.
